Experimental, developed by AI. Label Anything is still experimental and under active development, not production-ready software. It is written mostly by an AI coding assistant (Claude Code) with limited human oversight, code and documentation alike: expect mistakes, and check the results that matter to you. The problem format, the APIs of the language bindings and the placements themselves can change without deprecation. Try it and report what you find.

Label placement for charts, maps and diagrams, from any language. Label Anything decides where labels go: it places text, icons, or anything with a size next to selected points and areas of scatterplots, maps, node-link diagrams and illustrations. It avoids whatever you say should not be covered, draws leader lines when labels must sit at a distance, and never lets leaders cross.
